text: Write two versions of a summation, one recursive and one iterative, and find where the recursive one fails. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: static long sumRec(int n) { return n == 0 ? 0 : ___; }
static long sumLoop(int n) { long acc = 0; for (int i = n; i > 0; i--) ___; return acc; }
catch (___ e) { System.out.println("recursive version ran out of stack"); }
explanation: Verified: the loop prints 500000500000 and the recursion overflows. Both compute the same function; only one has a depth proportional to its input. Chapter 32 states the general rule — a recursion whose depth grows with the input has an input-size limit far below what memory suggests, while a recursion of depth log n is fine forever, which is why divide-and-conquer is safe and a linear walk is not.
